assumptions: The pilot measures the same quantity, on the same population, as the planned experiment.
Observations are independent within groups; the noncentral-t interval assumes normal errors.
limits: A small pilot gives a wide interval; sizing from the point estimate alone understates the samples needed when the true effect sits at the low end.
Pilot effects are biased upward when a pilot was continued because it looked promising.
bio.jane/contract.question: How large is the effect in pilot data, standardized, with a confidence interval, ready to size the full experiment?

description: The effect a power calculation needs, measured from a pilot instead of guessed: two groups of one measurement in a table, standardized as Hedges' g (default), Cohen's d or Glass's Δ with its noncentral-t confidence interval (effectsize 1.0.3, reproduced), and the two-sample t design sized at the estimate and at the interval limit nearest zero. A column can be subtracted row by row first (a reference gene's Ct, giving delta-Ct). Returns the `design` calculate_power takes: Cohen's d for the `t` test, the raw difference and SD for `t_raw`.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alternative.description: a two-sided interval, or one bounded on one side. Values: two.sided (Two-sided), less (Less (upper bound only)), greater (Greater (lower bound only)). Advanced.

ci.description: the confidence level of the interval.

estimator.description: Hedges' g corrects Cohen's d's small-sample bias by the exact J(df); Cohen's d is the uncorrected standardized difference; Glass's Δ standardizes by the reference group's SD alone, for when the treatment changes the spread. Values: hedges_g (Hedges' g), cohens_d (Cohen's d), glass_delta (Glass's Δ).

group.description: the group compared. Left unset, the second group to appear.

group_column.description: the column naming each row's group. Or give `groups`.

groups.description: one group label per data row, in row order, separated by commas, spaces or new lines, when the table has no group column.

paired.description: the two groups are the same subjects measured twice, paired by row order within each group. Only applies when estimator is hedges_g or cohens_d.

pooled_sd.description: standardize by the pooled SD (Student). Off averages the two variances, with Welch's df. Only applies when estimator is hedges_g or cohens_d.

power.description: size the design for this power; leave empty to estimate the effect only.

reference.description: the group it is compared against (the control). Left unset, the first group to appear.

subtract.description: a column subtracted from the measurement row by row before anything else: a reference gene's Ct (giving delta-Ct), a baseline.

table.description: the pilot: a header row, then one row per observation. Tab- or comma-separated.

name: estimate_effect_size

design.description: what calculate_power takes: the t test's d (`effect`), and the raw `difference` and `sd` for t_raw

groups.description: every group in the table: n, mean and SD of the measurement

interval.description: the confidence interval: level, low, high

sizing.description: pwr.t.test's sample size at the estimate and at the limit nearest zero, when power was given
